PIN_ERRLOC_APP.meaning: Invalid input data, nonexistent POID, or business policy rejection.
PIN_ERRLOC_APP.quick_check: Inspect input flist for invalid fields or policy validation failure.

PIN_ERRLOC_PCP.meaning: Socket or network transport failure between client/CM/DM.
PIN_ERRLOC_PCP.quick_check: Verify target daemon is running and port is reachable.

PIN_ERRLOC_PCM.meaning: Context initialization or connection pool allocation failure.
PIN_ERRLOC_PCM.quick_check: Check CM connection limits and client pin.conf pointers.

PIN_ERRLOC_CM.meaning: Opcode routing failure: missing fm_module directive or missing routing POID.

PIN_ERRLOC_FM.meaning: FList structure violates opcode specification (missing mandatory field).
PIN_ERRLOC_FM.quick_check: Verify required fields on input flist before opcode call.

PIN_ERRLOC_FLIST.meaning: Data type mismatch, NULL pointer, or out of memory in flist manipulation.
PIN_ERRLOC_FLIST.quick_check: Check pin_flist_get/put data types and NULL checks.

PIN_ERRLOC_POID.meaning: Malformed POID string, invalid DB number, or unallocated ID.
PIN_ERRLOC_POID.quick_check: Verify POID DB number (e.g. 0.0.0.1) and storable class name.

PIN_ERRLOC_DM.meaning: Database persistence failure or SQL constraint violation.
PIN_ERRLOC_DM.quick_check: Inspect dm_oracle.pinlog for companion ORA- code.

PIN_ERR_NOT_FOUND.description: Requested object, account, or field does not exist in database or flist.
likelyCauses: POID reference points to a deleted or uncommitted record
Field requested via pin_flist_get is not present on the flist
Account or service search returned zero matches
checks: Verify target POID exists in DB: 'testnap -> read <poid>'
Check pin_flist_get calls use PIN_RET_NULL or verify field presence first
Check search flist criteria and filter flags
resolutions: Ensure prerequisite parent record exists before querying child objects.
Add fallback handling when optional flist fields are missing.

PIN_ERR_MISSING_ARG.description: A required mandatory field is missing from the input flist.
likelyCauses: Input flist did not include PIN_FLD_POID or required business field
Policy opcode stripped a required field during preprocessing
Client passed an empty or partially populated flist
checks: Log input flist prior to opcode call: 'pin_flist_print(flist_p, cm.log)'
Verify opcode specification for mandatory input fields
Check custom policy FMs for dropped fields
resolutions: Populate all mandatory fields on input flist before dispatching opcode.

PIN_ERR_BAD_ARG.description: Field value is invalid, negative, or type does not match definition.
likelyCauses: Data type mismatch (e.g. passing PIN_FLDT_STR instead of PIN_FLDT_DECIMAL)
Negative quantity passed to balance or rating opcode
Invalid enum constant or unmapped status code
checks: Check pin_flist_put field type against ops/pin_*.h definition
Verify numeric values are within valid operational range
resolutions: Correct data type and range validation in calling application.

PIN_ERR_DUPLICATE.description: Attempted to insert a duplicate record violating unique constraint.
likelyCauses: Login name or account number already exists in BRM database
Concurrent batch jobs inserting duplicate transaction IDs
Sequence generator range exhausted or desynchronized
checks: Check dm_oracle.pinlog for matching ORA-00001 constraint name
Query database to check existing record with same key
resolutions: Check if transaction or account was already processed before retry.
Verify sequence generator values in /sequence storable class.

PIN_ERR_BAD_OPCODE.description: Opcode number received by CM is not mapped to any loaded FM module.
likelyCauses: Missing 'fm_module' entry in sys/cm/pin.conf
Custom shared library (.so) failed to load during CM startup
CM not restarted after editing pin.conf
Client opcode header out of sync with server
checks: Check sys/cm/pin.conf for '- cm fm_module <lib> <init_func>'
Check cm.pinlog for dlopen / shared object errors
Verify client header numerical value matches server PCM_OP_*
resolutions: Add missing FM directive to pin.conf and restart CM ('stop_cm && start_cm').

PIN_ERR_NAP_CONNECT_FAILED.description: Client cannot establish TCP connection with Connection Manager.
likelyCauses: CM process is stopped or crashed
Port mismatch between client pin.conf and CM pin.conf
CM max_cm_processes connection limit reached
Network firewall blocking TCP port
checks: Verify CM is running: 'ps -ef | grep cm' or Process Explorer
Verify CM port in sys/cm/pin.conf: '- cm cm_ports <port>'
Test connection: 'telnet <host> <port>'
resolutions: Start CM ('start_cm') or increase max_cm_processes in pin.conf.

PIN_ERR_STORAGE.description: Data Manager encountered a database or SQL execution failure.
likelyCauses: Database tablespace full or quota exceeded
Oracle listener down or database instance in restricted mode
Invalid schema credentials in sys/dm_oracle/pin.conf
checks: Inspect dm_oracle.pinlog to find companion ORA- code
Check Oracle alert log and tablespace free space
resolutions: Resolve underlying Oracle DB issue or tablespace allocation.

PIN_ERR_NO_MEM.description: Process memory exhausted during flist manipulation or query execution.
likelyCauses: Unbounded PCM_OP_SEARCH returning thousands of objects in memory
Memory leak in custom C/C++ FM module (unfreed flists)
checks: Check search flist flags: use PIN_SRCH_DISTINCT and limit result count
Verify pin_flist_destroy is called for all allocated flists
resolutions: Paginate large search queries and release flist memory using pin_flist_destroy.
